newsitem.title: USA: Pratt wins $115 million United engine deal.
newsitem.headline: Pratt wins $115 million United engine deal.

text.p: Jet engine maker Pratt & Whitney, a unit of United Technologies Corp., said Thursday it won a contract from UAL Corp.'s United Airlines worth about $115 million.
Pratt said United chose PW4000 engines for eight additional Boeing Co. 767-300 aircraft that the Chicago-based airline is purchasing.
The new 767s will be used on domestic routes to replace older United planes when delivery begins in May 1998, Pratt said.
Pratt, based in Hartford, Conn., said it will supply 16 installed and two spare PW4052 engines.
Some 1,800 of the engines are now in service with 70 customers around the world, Pratt said.
United Technologies' stock rose $1.75 to $86, while UAL gained 50 cents to $74.06 on the New York Stock Exchange.
